title: Cost Stewardship Sprint — Adaptive Inference Knobs & Guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Run a focused 6-week initiative (Cost Stewardship Sprint) to reduce hosted inference unit cost on 3 representative workloads by 15% without regressing P95 latency beyond 10% or user-visible quality. Scope includes adaptive batching defaults, prefix / KV cache policies, and 4-bit quantization pilot profiles. We will package knobs into an 'Adaptive Inference' config group in Console and the API so teams can opt-in with safe defaults.
objectives_and_okrs: O1: Reduce per-token cost for conversational and embed-heavy workloads by >=15% across target experiments
KR1.1: Deploy adaptive batching default that yields >=8% cost saving on conversational baseline
KR1.2: Ship KV cache policy tweaks that reduce repeated-token compute by >=6% on long-context workloads
KR1.3: Launch a conservative 4-bit quantization profile for two model families and measure quality delta <=2% on eval prompts
O2: Maintain reliability and quality guardrails
KR2.1: Keep P95 tail latency regression <=10% for production QPS profiles
KR2.2: No customer-facing incidents attributable to the initiative during rollout phase
success_metrics: Percent cost reduction (per-token compute) by workload: target 15%
Quality delta measured by eval Suite A: target <=2% regression
Adoption: 30% of internal Redwood teams opt into adaptive config within 8 weeks of rollout
scope_included: Adaptive batching policy (server-side defaults + per-route override)
KV/prefix cache policy presets and eviction heuristics
Conservative 4-bit quantization profiles (model-specific) and validation harness
Console UX to expose 'Adaptive Inference' toggle and rollout controls
Monitoring dashboards and automated regression alerts tied to eval sets
out_of_scope: New compiler-level kernel changes (research will feed future sprints)
Major model architecture changes or retraining
milestones: Week 1: Finish experiment design, select 3 canonical workloads and baseline metrics (conversational, summarization, embeddings)
Week 2-3: Engineering implements adaptive batching and cache presets; QA runs synthetic traffic tests
Week 4: Pilot quantization profiles on staging; run end-to-end evals and A/B tests
Week 5: Canary rollout to 10% of host tenants/internal apps, monitor regressions and rollback windows
Week 6: Post-mortem, docs, console release, and handbook entry for SRE/CS teams
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks: aggregated cost reduction >=15% on sample workloads
Quality: eval Suite A shows <=2% regression for conversational outputs
Observability: dashboards with per-model per-route cost & latency available in Console
Rollout controls: canary, abort, and rollback implemented and tested
Docs: runbook and customer-facing knowledge base article drafted

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: quality regression from quantization. Mitigation: conservative profiles, synthetic and human evals, slow canary rollout.
Risk: increased latency from batching under low QPS. Mitigation: dynamic max latency bound per route; fallback to small-batch path.
Risk: cache churn on multi-tenant hosts reduces effectiveness. Mitigation: tenant-aware caching heuristics and shard-local counters.
Risk: user confusion around defaults. Mitigation: clear console labels, recommended defaults, and opt-out instructions in KB
